Modern.brandDescription: Moose Test is an agent-evaluation platform that treats AI agents the way crash labs treat cars: standardized evasive scenarios, pass or fail, filmed and published. Every agent release runs the same suite of adversarial swerves — ambiguous instructions, hostile tools, mid-task interruptions — before it is allowed near a customer. Moose Test scores are public, versioned, and reproducible, so a passing grade means something across the industry, not just inside one dashboard.
Modern.scope: Moose Test covers scenario-suite authoring, trajectory-level scoring, regression gating in CI, and a public scoreboard of anonymized pass rates by agent category. It does not build agents, host models, or sell consulting — it runs the test track.
Modern.brandNameRationale: The moose test (älgtest) is the real Swedish evasive-maneuver trial that famously flipped the Mercedes A-Class in 1997 and forced a redesign — a standardized swerve that separates cars that look safe from cars that are safe. Borrowing it names exactly what agent evals should be: one canonical, public, embarrassing-if-you-fail scenario suite.
Modern.industrySummary: Through 2025 the agent-eval market pivoted from saturated static benchmarks toward trajectory- and scenario-based evaluation, as enterprises discovered that MMLU-style scores predict nothing about a booking agent that wires money. Eval tooling became a funded category in its own right — Braintrust, Langfuse, and Patronus all raised on the thesis that evals gate deployment the way tests gate merges. By 2026 procurement teams increasingly ask vendors for eval evidence before pilots, and the open question is whose scenario suites become the industry's shared yardstick.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Patronus AI (patronus.ai) sells automated LLM evaluation and safety testing to enterprises. Langfuse (langfuse.com) is the open-source LLM engineering platform with eval and tracing primitives. HoneyHive (honeyhive.ai) covers agent observability and evaluation for production teams. Moose Test differs by making the scenario suite itself the product — standardized, public, and comparable across vendors, rather than a private dashboard per team.
Modern.positioningStatement: The standardized crash test for AI agents: one public suite, one pass line, no partial credit.
Modern.positioningRationale: Private evals let every team grade its own homework, which is why agent incidents keep surprising buyers. A public, versioned, pass/fail standard converts evaluation from an internal hygiene task into a market signal — and the brand that owns the standard owns the category's trust.

targetAudience.primary: Eval leads, staff engineers, and heads of platform at companies shipping production agents — people whose name is on the deploy button. Modern.brandDescription: Shelfmark is retrieval infrastructure built on a librarian's premise: a document you cannot locate might as well not exist. The platform combines hybrid dense-sparse indexing, reranking, and freshness guarantees under a recall SLA — a contractual floor on how often the right passage comes back. Shelfmark publishes recall figures per corpus type the way food companies publish nutrition labels, so teams know what the index actually does before they build an agent on top of it.
Modern.brandNameRationale: A shelfmark is the real library-science term for the code that records exactly where a book lives — used at the British Library and the Bodleian for centuries before 'vector search' existed. It anchors the brand in the oldest retrieval discipline on earth: things that are findable because someone gave them an address.
Modern.industrySummary: Retrieval infrastructure consolidated hard through 2025: hybrid search became the default over pure vector similarity, rerankers moved from optional to assumed, and object-storage-first architectures reset cost expectations for large corpora. Million-token context windows triggered a 'RAG is dead' debate that production teams settled quickly — long context is a complement, not a replacement, once freshness, permissioning, and per-query cost enter the picture. Into 2026 the buying criterion is shifting from raw ANN benchmarks to end-to-end retrieval quality on the customer's own documents.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Pinecone (pinecone.io) is the managed vector-database incumbent with serverless indexing. Turbopuffer (turbopuffer.com) resets the cost curve with object-storage-native search used by fast-growing AI products. Vespa (vespa.ai) offers the heavyweight open platform for hybrid search and ranking at scale. Shelfmark differs by selling a measured outcome — recall under SLA on your corpus — rather than an index you must tune and benchmark yourself.
Modern.positioningStatement: The retrieval layer that signs its name to a recall number.
Modern.positioningRationale: Every retrieval vendor claims quality; almost none will put a floor on it in a contract. Committing to measured recall per corpus converts an infrastructure commodity into an accountable service, and it forces the internal engineering discipline that the category mostly fakes.

targetAudience.primary: Engineers who have shipped one RAG system that embarrassed them. They are platform and search engineers at AI-native products and enterprises with large private corpora, past the tutorial phase, and now accountable for why the agent cited the 2019 policy instead of the current one. They think in recall@k and cost per thousand queries.

Modern.story: Shelfmark started when its founders — one ex-search infrastructure engineer, one former academic librarian turned data engineer — watched an enterprise pilot fail because the agent retrieved a superseded contract clause. The company they were helping had every document; it just had no idea where anything was. The pair rebuilt the pipeline around an old library principle: catalog first, search second, and never return an item without its provenance. The recall SLA came later, when a customer asked, 'Can you put that in the contract?' and they realized no one in the industry ever had.

Modern.brandDescription: Strowger is a voice-agent platform engineered around a single obsession: the first 700 milliseconds of a phone call. Interruption handling, barge-in, turn-taking, and time-to-first-word are tuned and published per release, because callers forgive a wrong answer faster than a slow one. Strowger gives engineering teams the telephony stack, the speech pipeline, and the latency budget tooling to run agents that feel like the fastest operator you ever reached.
Modern.scope: Strowger provides the real-time speech-to-speech pipeline, SIP/telephony integration, turn-taking engine, and per-call latency observability. Agent logic, CRM integrations, and conversation design remain the customer's — Strowger runs the line, not the script.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Almon B. Strowger was the Kansas City undertaker who patented the automatic telephone exchange in 1889 — legend says because a local operator was diverting his business calls to a rival. His stepping switch removed the human middleman from the phone call; the name anchors the brand in the founding act of call automation.
Modern.industrySummary: Voice AI crossed its credibility threshold in 2025: native speech-to-speech models cut round-trip latency under a second, and platforms like Vapi and Retell turned voice agents into an assemble-not-build market for support lines, scheduling, and outbound qualification. The differentiator war moved from 'does it talk' to conversational mechanics — barge-in, endpointing, handling the caller who interrupts twice in a sentence. Into 2026, telephony-grade reliability and per-call economics are deciding enterprise deals, while regulators sharpen disclosure rules for AI callers.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Vapi (vapi.ai) is the developer platform for building and deploying voice agents fast. Retell AI (retellai.com) targets contact-center-grade voice agents with strong telephony features. LiveKit (livekit.io) supplies the open real-time infrastructure many voice stacks are built on. Strowger differs by making latency a published, contractual spec — every release ships with time-to-first-word numbers — rather than one feature among many.
Modern.positioningStatement: The voice-agent platform that treats latency as the product.
Modern.positioningRationale: In voice, delay is the uncanny valley: 300 extra milliseconds reads as evasion, and callers hang up on evasion. Owning the latency spec — measured, published, guaranteed — claims the one dimension every buyer can hear in the first five seconds of a demo call.

They measure abandonment rates, know their peak-hour concurrency, and have been burned by a demo that fell apart on real calls.

When they dug into telephone history for a name, they found Almon Strowger, the undertaker who automated the exchange because he could not trust the operator, and recognized the same impatience that had driven them to build.

Luxury.brandDescription: Hobbs & Bramah is a private AI red-teaming house retained by frontier labs, banks, and governments to break their models before deployment. Prompt injection held its place atop the OWASP LLM risk list while automated attack generation — pioneered commercially by Haize Labs and open-sourced through tools like promptfoo — industrialized what had been artisanal jailbreaking. The premium tier of the market now belongs to human expert teams handling frontier deployments where an automated sweep is table stakes, not assurance.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Haize Labs (haizelabs.com) automates adversarial testing and jailbreak discovery at scale. Lakera (lakera.ai) pairs its Gandalf-honed attack data with runtime defense products. HiddenLayer (hiddenlayer.com) covers the broader ML-security platform for enterprises. Creative.tagline: Give your agent somewhere to keep it.
Creative.brandDescription: Simonides is a memory engine for AI agents built on the architecture of the memory palace: instead of a flat vector store of everything ever said, agents get structured rooms — entities, episodes, preferences, commitments — with deliberate placement, decay, and recall. What matters gets a location; what doesn't gets forgotten on schedule; what's recalled arrives with the context of where it lives. Simonides turns agents from brilliant amnesiacs into colleagues who remember why.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Simonides of Ceos, the Greek poet, stepped out of a banquet hall moments before its roof collapsed — and identified the crushed guests by remembering where each had sat. From that catastrophe he derived the method of loci, the memory-palace technique that carried human memory for 2,500 years. The name plants agent memory in its true lineage: memory is architecture, not storage.
Creative.industrySummary: Agent memory became the defining infrastructure race of late 2025: as agents moved from stateless chat to persistent work, teams discovered that context windows are working memory, not memory, and a specialist layer emerged — Letta from the MemGPT research line, Mem0's rapid open-source ascent, Zep's temporal knowledge graphs. The hard problems shifted from storage to editorial judgment: what to keep, what to decay, how memories compose across sessions without contradiction. Into 2026, memory is emerging as the retention moat of agent products — users stay where they are remembered — with privacy regulation shaping what remembering is allowed to mean.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Letta (letta.com) commercializes the MemGPT research lineage for stateful agents. Mem0 (mem0.ai) drives the popular open-source memory layer for AI applications. Zep (getzep.com) builds temporal knowledge-graph memory for agent systems. Simonides differs on architecture-as-doctrine: opinionated memory rooms with placement, decay schedules, and spatially structured recall, rather than a general store the developer must curate.
Creative.positioningStatement: The memory palace for agents: structured rooms, deliberate forgetting, recall with context.
Creative.positioningRationale: Flat memory stores make remembering cheap and recall noisy — the exact failure the method of loci solved for humans. An opinionated spatial architecture differentiates on quality of recall rather than quantity of storage, and the 2,500-year-old brand story explains the technical thesis in one image.

Structure, placement, deliberate decay — everything the ancients knew, nothing their stack did. They rebuilt memory as rooms instead of rows, and named the company for the poet who walked out of the rubble remembering where everyone sat.

Creative.tagline: Annotation is a trade. We treat it like one.
Creative.brandDescription: Journeyman & Daughters is a data-labeling guild: annotators are salaried craftspeople with apprenticeships, published day rates, and names that appear in the model cards their work trains. The guild takes commissions in domains where judgment is the product — medical imaging, legal reasoning, safety evaluation — and refuses piecework pricing on principle. Journeyman & Daughters exists to prove that the industry's most invisible labor is actually its scarcest skill.

Creative.brandNameRationale: In the medieval guild system, the journeyman was the credentialed craftsman between apprentice and master — paid by the day (journée), carrying papers that proved training, free to take his skill wherever it was valued. Flipping the patriarchal '& Sons' to '& Daughters' plants the old structure in the present tense: same standards, new trade, everyone's craft counted.
Creative.industrySummary: Data labeling's center of gravity moved decisively upmarket through 2025: Meta's $14B-scale investment in Scale AI triggered a customer exodus that scattered frontier work across Surge, Labelbox, and specialist vendors, while post-training demand shifted from bulk annotation toward expert judgment — physicians grading clinical reasoning, lawyers ranking arguments, engineers demonstrating agentic tasks. Rates for frontier-quality human data rose even as commodity labeling automated away. Into 2026, labor conditions and annotator provenance are entering procurement questionnaires, and 'who exactly produced this data' has become a diligence question with money attached.

Radical labor transparency converts an ethics posture into a quality argument: named, salaried, credentialed craftspeople produce better judgment than anonymous piecework, and can prove it.

They resolve what the night brings, they know exactly what they're not entitled to decide, and they leave a handover so clean your morning coffee goes cold before you find a problem in it. Sleep.
